instruction: Make the title 'Presentation Instruction' bold and set its font size to 16.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully converted all uppercase text to lowercase using Ctrl+A to select all, then Format > Text > lowercase, then Ctrl+S to save. Completed in 7 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select all text (Ctrl+A), navigate LibreOffice Writer menus (Format > Text > case options), save documents (Ctrl+S). Comfortable with text formatting operations.
metadata.task_rationale: Different formatting operation on the same document. The model demonstrated ability to select text and apply formatting via menus. Making title bold and changing font size tests similar menu navigation skills.
metadata.explanation: Task requires making the first paragraph bold and changing its font size to 16pt. Getter reads the first paragraph's formatting properties (bold, font size). Metric gives 0.5 for bold, 0.5 for correct font size.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the first paragraph (title) of the docx file and extracts bold status and font sizes from runs.
Metric correctly awards 0.5 for bold and 0.5 for font size matching 16pt, covering both instruction requirements.
Expected parameter handling is correct: metric receives rules dict directly and accesses expected.get('expected_size', 16).
Postconfig saves the file with Ctrl+S before getter reads it, ensuring state is fresh.

Minor issue: run.bold can be None (inherited from style) and 'not None' evaluates to True, so style-inherited bold would be incorrectly reported as not bold. In practice, explicit formatting via UI sets run.bold=True, so this is unlikely to cause issues.
Minor issue: if font_sizes list is empty (size set at style level only), no font size points are awarded. Unlikely after explicit UI formatting but a possible edge case.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider handling run.bold=None in the getter by checking 'if run.bold is False' instead of 'if not run.bold' to properly handle style-inherited bold.
Consider adding a fallback in the getter to check paragraph-level or style-level font size if no run-level sizes are found.
